Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Power Holdings Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Power Holdings' Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer; David Kim, Chief Strategy Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
1. Strong customer growth and usage trends across residential, commercial, and industrial segments.
2. Advancements in grid modernization and smart grid initiatives.
3. Steady rate base growth supported by key investments.
4. Positive updates on regulatory rate case filings and outcomes.
5. Effective storm response and recovery efforts.
6. Proactive management perspectives on industry trends and challenges.

Let me provide some more detail on these six key aspects.

First, on customer growth and usage trends. Total customer count grew 2.8% year-over-year to 4.72 million, driven by organic additions in our high-growth Southeast and Texas footprints. Weather-normalized retail sales increased 3.4% to 28.5 million MWh, outpacing the U.S. utility average of 1.9% as reported by the Edison Electric Institute. This marks our eighth consecutive quarter of positive load growth, with a compounded annual growth rate of 4.1% over the past three years. Key drivers include EV adoption at 12% penetration in our residential base, industrial reshoring, and the rise of AI-driven data centers, which added over 1,200 MW of contracted load in Q3.

In the residential segment, customers expanded 3.2% year-over-year to 3.85 million, with net additions of 118,000, concentrated in Florida and Georgia where population inflows exceed 1.5% annually per U.S. Census data. Usage per customer rose 1.8% on a weather-normalized basis to 1,045 kWh per month, reflecting electrification trends. Electric vehicle charging now accounts for 8% of residential peak demand, up from 4% last year, supported by EV-ready rate pilots with over 45,000 participants. Heat pump adoption surged 22% in milder climate zones, driven by IRA incentives and our rebate programs similar to those of Duke Energy and Southern Company. Texas residential load grew 5.1% amid the housing boom, while Northeast exposure was tempered by mild summer cooling degree days at 850 versus the 10-year average of 1,020. We've deployed 250,000 advanced metering infrastructure units this year, enabling time-of-use rates that shifted 15% of residential load off-peak, reducing strain on peaker plants. We project 2.5-3.0% annual customer growth through 2027, with usage per customer climbing another 2% CAGR as rooftop solar—now at 7% DER penetration—pairs with virtual power plant aggregation via partnerships like Google Nest.

Commercial customer growth was 1.9% year-over-year to 785,000, but usage rose 2.7% to 8.2 million MWh. Retail strip centers and offices were flat at 0.5% amid hybrid work, but data centers contributed 42% of growth, securing 850 MW of new hyperscaler contracts with Microsoft and Meta, similar to Dominion Energy's Virginia deals. In Southeast markets, data center load density hit 150 MW per site with PUE ratings below 1.3 thanks to liquid cooling. Texas ERCOT saw 18% commercial usage growth from crypto mining rebounds. Challenges in California-adjacent areas include rooftop solar offsetting 12% of load, addressed by 300 MW of BESS co-location. Demand response programs curtailed 120 MW during peaks, saving $45 million in capacity. We expect 3-4% usage growth in 2025, driven by data centers.

Industrial customers grew 1.4% to 85,000, with 6.2% usage increase to 11.8 million MWh. Onshoring in semiconductors and EVs added 450 MW, like TSMC's Arizona fabs and Rivian expansions. Steel and chemicals in the Midwest grew 9% with CHIPS Act funding, demand per customer at 142 MWh per month. Texas jumped 11% from LNG terminals, Ohio Valley from manufacturing. Electrification via HVDC supports 25% of load from renewables, with 50 MW electrolyzer pilots. Dynamic line rating on 200 miles unlocked 15% capacity. FERC Order 2222 enabled 200 MW behind-the-meter storage. We're allocating $2.4 billion over five years for grid hardening, targeting 1,200 MW new industrial attach rate, with 5-7% CAGR despite risks like smelter curtailments.

Second, grid modernization and smart grid initiatives. We operate a 45,000-mile T&D network serving 8.5 million customers across Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, and Southeast. In Q3, we deployed $285 million in smart grid investments, year-to-date $820 million—up 22%—28% of $2.9 billion 2024 capex. This includes a $450 million Grid Modernization Roadmap approved by FERC and PUCs in New York, Pennsylvania, and Virginia. We've reduced SAIDI 15% to 85 minutes and SAIFI 18% to 0.92, saving $42 million in O&M via automated fault isolation, cutting penalties 35%.

Pillars include AMI with 4.2 million smart meters—75% Northeast penetration—using Landis+Gyr Revelo integrated with Oracle NMS, enabling TOU for 2.8 million customers, shifting 12% peak demand and saving $18 million. In Mid-Atlantic, AMI optimizes LMP, reducing congestion 9% or $22 million. Grid automation upgraded 65% of 34.5/69 kV feeders with Siemens SIPROTEC 5 and GE ADMS FLISR on 1,200 feeders, slashing restoration to under 12 minutes—like during August hurricane remnants, restoring 92% in 30 minutes. Southeast benefits for data center uptime. DERMS from ABB manages 1.2 GW solar/storage, orchestrating 250 MW VPPs with Sunrun/Tesla, generating $14 million ancillary revenues. Bidirectional EV charging pilots add 50 MW V2G.

We're at 75% AMI vs. U.S. 50%, targeting 95% by 2026. $1.2 billion capex yields $0.45 EPS from 2026 at 6.5% ROE. Regulatory tailwinds like REV and Clean Economy Act. Supply chain mitigated with Eaton/Schneider; $65 million cybersecurity with Dragos thwarted attacks. Phase 2 2025: edge AI, 500 MW BESS.

Third, rate base growth. As of Q3 end, consolidated rate base at $26.4 billion, up 6.2% YoY from $24.9 billion, at upper end of 5-7% band, 5.8% CAGR since 2020. Trailing AFUDC added $185 million. 2023 placed $1.8 billion in service; 2024 on track for $2.0 billion from $2.7 billion capex—60% T&D, 25% renewables/storage.

Drivers: Southeast commercial load 4.5% YoY from data centers (1,200 MW), justifying $850 million T&D. Residential EV adds 2%. Georgia PSC 2023 case added $1.2 billion CWIP; Florida Everglades Solar 100% CWIP at 10.25% ROE. NC tracker $250 million YTD; pending dockets $3.5 billion. Renewables 35% mix, 1.1 GW added; Falcon 300 MW BESS, resiliency program $400 million. Southeast 7% growth vs. Texas 4%. IRA $150 million PTCs. Target 10-12% returns >7.5% WACC; 5-7% CAGR to $32-34 billion by 2028.

Fourth, regulatory rate case updates. Rate cases fund $4.2 billion capex for renewables, hardening, storage. Indiana IURC approved 96% of $520 million request—$498 million rate base, 10.25% ROE, 100% CWIP for 500 MW wind, $142 million revenue, $0.28 EPS 2025. Pennsylvania PUC $215 million on $1.8 billion, full AFUDC Susquehanna uprate, 10.35% ROE, $0.15 EPS. Ohio settlement 98% recovery, 10.4% ROE, PBR EV pilots. Texas $750 million plan for resilience; Virginia $320 million offshore. Midwest 10.3% ROEs; de-risks $12 billion capex, 10.4% blended ROE by 2026.

Fifth, storm response for Hurricane Zeta. Landfall Category 3 Florida Panhandle October 15, 1.2 million peak outages. EOC 72 hours early, 5,000 workers from 18 states via EEI, 150 drones for assessment. Restored 50% in 24 hours, 90% in 48, 99.5% in five days—better than Southeast average. Critical infra under six hours with 150 MW mobile gen. Florida $120 million substations; Gulf steel monopoles limited damage. CMI 450 vs. 620 average. Gross cost $285 million, net $45 million or 3 cents/share after $140 million insurance, deferral riders. Down 20% from Eta via securitization. BESS islanded 12 hours. Strategy: Predict with Palantir, Protect $800 million 2025 hardening, Recover with assessment center. Positions ahead of peers.

Sixth, industry trends. Demand 4.5-5% U.S. annual from data centers (35 GW by 2030), EVs; our load 6.2% Q2. Renewables LCOE solar $25/MWh; IRA funds 2.5 GW pipeline 12% IRR; 800 MW offshore. Challenges: intermittency, queues 2.5 TW, transformers delayed; 1.2 GWh BESS colocated. Policy: nuclear/coal risks 40 GW; PJM auctions $269/MW-day. ERCOT volatility, PJM/MISO SMRs NuScale, Southeast nuclear/hydrogen. Natgas $2.50, uranium $90/lb. $4.5 billion FCF for 8-10% EPS, 50% carbon-free 2030, iron-air storage.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss the financials.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. For Q3 2024, we reported earnings per share of $1.25 and revenue of $2.8 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $850 million, primarily focused on grid modernization and renewable expansions. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders. We anticipate EPS growth of 7-9% in 2025.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. Let me provide an update on the operational front. We are seeing improved efficiency in our natural gas combined-cycle power plants due to the implementation of advanced digital controls. This has resulted in a 12% increase in output. Our outage rates are also down 20%.

David Kim: Thank you, Lisa. Turning to our long-term strategy, we are actively exploring opportunities in the battery energy storage systems space. We believe this will be a key driver of future growth. We are also evaluating potential acquisitions in the Southeast U.S. market.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, David. From a technology perspective, we are making significant investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity. We recently deployed an AI-driven threat detection platform to enhance our defenses against cyber threats.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Michael, Lisa, David, and Elena. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Miller with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Miller: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for customer growth in the data center segment?

Sarah Thompson: Certainly. Data centers are a multi-decade driver, with 850 MW new hyperscaler contracts in Q3 contributing 42% of commercial growth. Southeast density at 150 MW/site, Texas 18% usage rise. We're allocating grid hardening for 1,200 MW attach rate, projecting 3-4% commercial growth skewed to high-load users, supported by BESS co-location and demand response saving $45 million.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: What is your outlook for rate base growth amid regulatory changes?

Michael Chen: Strong tailwinds here. Rate base up 6.2% to $26.4 billion, guiding 5-7% CAGR to $32-34 billion by 2028 from $12-14 billion capex. Load growth justifies T&D, regulatory like Georgia CWIP adds $1.2 billion. IRA credits offset costs, targeting 10-12% returns.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Hayes with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Robert Hayes: How are you mitigating risks related to storm frequency?

Lisa Patel: We've built resilience: Zeta response exceeded benchmarks with 99.5% restoration in five days via EEI mutual aid, drones, OMS. $800 million 2025 hardening—undergrounding, smart substations, microgrids. Riders and insurance limit EPS hit to 3 cents, BESS/VPPs enhance recovery.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in Q3 2024, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Apex Power Holdings for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Apex Power Holdings.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
